    19	/-- The parameter part of Hypothesis `H:homog`, with `a = α₀`. -/
    20	def Homog (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) : Prop :=
    21	  (d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) ∧ 0 < a ∧ a < 1 ∧ a + alpha < 2 ∧
    22	    ((0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1))
    23	
    24	/-- The `γ`-interval `0 < γ < min(1/2, (2-α)/2)` is nonempty. -/
    25	theorem gamma_interval_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    26	    ∃ γ : ℝ, 0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2) := by
    27	  obtain ⟨-, ha0, -, hthr, -⟩ := h
    28	  have hm : 0 < min (1 / 2 : ℝ) ((2 - alpha) / 2) :=
    29	    lt_min (by norm_num) (by linarith)
    30	  exact ⟨min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2) / 2, by linarith, by linarith⟩
    31	
    32	/-- The `(θ, β)`-interval `1/2 < θ < β < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-α)/2)` is nonempty. -/
    33	theorem theta_beta_interval_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    34	    ∃ θ β : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2) := by
    35	  obtain ⟨-, -, ha1, hthr, -⟩ := h
    36	  set m := min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2) with hm
    37	  have hm' : 1 / 2 < m := lt_min (by linarith) (by linarith)
    38	  exact ⟨1 / 2 + (m - 1 / 2) / 3, 1 / 2 + 2 * (m - 1 / 2) / 3,
    39	    by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩
    40	
    41	/-- `E:driver-parameters`: "The strict intervals are nonempty", i.e. there are
    42	`γ, θ, β` with `0 < γ < min(1/2, (2-α)/2)` and
    43	`1/2 < θ < β < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-α)/2)`. -/
    44	theorem parameters_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    45	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
    46	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2)) := by
    47	  obtain ⟨γ, hγ⟩ := gamma_interval_nonempty d alpha a h
    48	  obtain ⟨θ, β, hθβ⟩ := theta_beta_interval_nonempty d alpha a h
    49	  exact ⟨γ, θ, β, hγ, hθβ⟩
    50	
    51	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.DriverParameters

     5	/-!
     6	# Scalar power estimates (manuscript `L:gaussian-scalar-powers`)
     7	
     8	Source: `notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex` at commit `ba01d98`, Lemma
     9	`L:gaussian-scalar-powers` (statement lines 13--28, proof lines 30--48).
    10	
    11	* `weighted_power`     -- (E:gaussian-weighted-power), weighted AM--GM.
    12	* `integer_power`      -- (E:gaussian-integer-power), natural-number powers.
    13	* `finite_holder`      -- finite Hölder with exponents `m` and `m/(m-1)`.
    14	* `expectation_rpow_le` -- `E Z^r ≤ F^r` for `Z ≥ 0`, `F = E Z`, `0 < r < 1`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	@[expose] public section
    18	
    19	noncomputable section
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	open MeasureTheory
    24	
    25	namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.GaussianScalarPowers
    26	
    27	/-- Part (1), (E:gaussian-weighted-power): for `0 < θ < 1` and `u, v ≥ 0`,
    28	`u^θ v^(1-θ) ≤ θ u + (1-θ) v` (real powers). -/
    29	theorem weighted_power (θ u v : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ1 : θ < 1)
    30	    (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hv : 0 ≤ v) :
    31	    u ^ θ * v ^ (1 - θ) ≤ θ * u + (1 - θ) * v :=
    32	  Real.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted hθ0.le (by linarith) hu hv (by ring)
    33	
    34	/-- Part (2), (E:gaussian-integer-power): for integers `L > 0`, `0 ≤ q ≤ L` and real
    35	`x, y`, `|x|^q |y|^(L-q) ≤ (q/L)|x|^L + ((L-q)/L)|y|^L` (natural-number powers,
    36	so `a^0 = 1`). -/
    37	theorem integer_power (L q : ℕ) (hL : 0 < L) (hqL : q ≤ L) (x y : ℝ) :
    38	    |x| ^ q * |y| ^ (L - q) ≤
    39	      (q : ℝ) / L * |x| ^ L + ((L : ℝ) - q) / L * |y| ^ L := by
    40	  have hLpos : (0 : ℝ) < L := by exact_mod_cast hL
    41	  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos q with rfl | hq0
    42	  · simp [hLpos.ne']
    43	  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hqL with rfl | hqlt
    44	  · simp [hLpos.ne']
    45	  -- 0 < q < L: apply `weighted_power` with θ = q/L, u = |x|^L, v = |y|^L.
    46	  have hqpos : (0 : ℝ) < q := by exact_mod_cast hq0
    47	  have hqltR : (q : ℝ) < L := by exact_mod_cast hqlt
    48	  set θ : ℝ := (q : ℝ) / L with hθ
    49	  have hθ0 : 0 < θ := div_pos hqpos hLpos
    50	  have hθ1 : θ < 1 := (div_lt_one hLpos).2 hqltR
    51	  have key := weighted_power θ (|x| ^ L) (|y| ^ L) hθ0 hθ1 (by positivity) (by positivity)
    52	  have h1 : (|x| ^ L) ^ θ = |x| ^ q := by
    53	    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (abs_nonneg x), hθ,
    54	      mul_div_cancel₀ _ hLpos.ne', Real.rpow_natCast]
    55	  have h2 : (|y| ^ L) ^ (1 - θ) = |y| ^ (L - q) := by
    56	    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_mul (abs_nonneg y), hθ,
    57	      ← Real.rpow_natCast, Nat.cast_sub hqL]
    58	    congr 1
    59	    field_simp
    60	  have h3 : 1 - θ = ((L : ℝ) - q) / L := by rw [hθ]; field_simp
    61	  rw [h1, h2, h3] at key
    62	  exact key
    63	
    64	/-- Part (3), finite Hölder for nonnegative finite sequences with exponents `m` and
    65	`m/(m-1)`, `m > 1`. -/
    66	theorem finite_holder {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (a b : ι → ℝ) (m : ℝ) (hm : 1 < m)
    67	    (ha : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ a i) (hb : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ b i) :
    68	    ∑ i ∈ s, a i * b i ≤
    69	      (∑ i ∈ s, a i ^ m) ^ (1 / m) *
    70	        (∑ i ∈ s, b i ^ (m / (m - 1))) ^ ((m - 1) / m) := by
    71	  have hm0 : 0 < m := by linarith
    72	  have hm1 : 0 < m - 1 := by linarith
    73	  have hconj : m.HolderConjugate (m / (m - 1)) := by
    74	    rw [Real.holderConjugate_iff]
    75	    refine ⟨hm, ?_⟩
    76	    field_simp
    77	    ring
    78	  have h := Real.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg s hconj ha hb
    79	  have hexp : 1 / (m / (m - 1)) = (m - 1) / m := by field_simp
    80	  rw [hexp] at h
    81	  exact h
    82	
    83	/-- Pointwise bound used for integrability in part (4): `z^r ≤ r z + (1 - r)`. -/
    84	private lemma rpow_le_affine (z r : ℝ) (hz : 0 ≤ z) (hr0 : 0 < r) (hr1 : r < 1) :
    85	    z ^ r ≤ r * z + (1 - r) := by
    86	  have := weighted_power r z 1 hr0 hr1 hz zero_le_one
    87	  simpa using this
    88	
    89	/-- Part (4): if `Z ≥ 0` a.s. has finite expectation `F = E Z` (on a probability space)
    90	and `0 < r < 1`, then `Z^r` is integrable and `E Z^r ≤ F^r`. -/
    91	theorem expectation_rpow_le {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω)
    92	    [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (Z : Ω → ℝ) (hZ : Integrable Z μ) (hZnn : 0 ≤ᵐ[μ] Z)
    93	    (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 < r) (hr1 : r < 1) :
    94	    Integrable (fun ω => Z ω ^ r) μ ∧ ∫ ω, Z ω ^ r ∂μ ≤ (∫ ω, Z ω ∂μ) ^ r := by
    95	  set F := ∫ ω, Z ω ∂μ with hF
    96	  have hint : Integrable (fun ω => Z ω ^ r) μ := by
    97	    refine Integrable.mono' ((hZ.const_mul r).add (integrable_const (1 - r)))
    98	      (hZ.aestronglyMeasurable.aemeasurable.pow_const r).aestronglyMeasurable ?_
    99	    filter_upwards [hZnn] with ω hω
   100	    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hω r)]
   101	    exact rpow_le_affine (Z ω) r hω hr0 hr1
   102	  refine ⟨hint, ?_⟩
   103	  have hF0 : 0 ≤ F := integral_nonneg_of_ae hZnn
   104	  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hF0 with hFz | hFpos
   105	  · -- F = 0 gives Z = 0 a.s.
   106	    have hZ0 : Z =ᵐ[μ] 0 := (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae hZnn hZ).1 hFz.symm
   107	    have : ∫ ω, Z ω ^ r ∂μ = 0 := by
   108	      rw [integral_eq_zero_of_ae]
   109	      filter_upwards [hZ0] with ω hω
   110	      simp [hω, Real.zero_rpow hr0.ne']
   111	    rw [this, ← hFz, Real.zero_rpow hr0.ne']
   112	  · -- F > 0: apply part (1) to u = Z/F, v = 1, θ = r, and integrate.
   113	    have hpt : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Z ω ^ r ≤ F ^ r * (r * (Z ω / F) + (1 - r)) := by
   114	      filter_upwards [hZnn] with ω hω
   115	      have h1 := rpow_le_affine (Z ω / F) r (div_nonneg hω hF0) hr0 hr1
   116	      have h2 : Z ω ^ r = F ^ r * (Z ω / F) ^ r := by
   117	        rw [Real.div_rpow hω hF0, mul_div_cancel₀]
   118	        exact (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hFpos r).ne'
   119	      rw [h2]
   120	      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 (Real.rpow_nonneg hF0 r)
   121	    have hrhs : Integrable (fun ω => F ^ r * (r * (Z ω / F) + (1 - r))) μ :=
   122	      (((hZ.div_const F).const_mul r).add (integrable_const (1 - r))).const_mul _
   123	    calc ∫ ω, Z ω ^ r ∂μ ≤ ∫ ω, F ^ r * (r * (Z ω / F) + (1 - r)) ∂μ :=
   124	          integral_mono_ae hint hrhs hpt
   125	      _ = F ^ r * (r * (F / F) + (1 - r)) := by
   126	          rw [integral_const_mul, integral_add ((hZ.div_const F).const_mul r)
   127	            (integrable_const (1 - r)), integral_const_mul,
   128	            integral_div, integral_const]
   129	          simp [← hF]
   130	      _ = F ^ r := by rw [div_self hFpos.ne']; ring
   131	
   132	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.GaussianScalarPowers

     4	Lemma `L:gram-scalar-algebra` of `notes/integrated_positive_gram.tex`
     5	(manuscript revision ba01d98): the scalar square-root duality, the Hilbert
     6	completed-square identity and inequality, and the finite Gram identity with
     7	`C_ij = ⟪k_i, k_j⟫` (the section's defining line).
     8	
     9	The manuscript works in a real Hilbert space. Completeness is not used, so the
    10	statements are made for any real inner product space; this is a weakening of
    11	the hypotheses, not a strengthening. The section's standing assumptions
    12	`C_ij ≥ 0`, `ℓ_i > 0`, `b_i ≥ 0` are not used by the lemma and are omitted.
    13	-/
    14	module
    15	
    16	public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
    17	public import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt
    18	public import Mathlib.Tactic
    19	
    20	@[expose] public section
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators
    25	
    26	universe u v
    27	
    28	namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.GramScalarAlgebra
    29	
    30	/-- `E:gram-sqrt-dual`: for real `ℓ`, `w > 0` and `t ≥ 0`,
    31	`2 ℓ √t ≤ ℓ² / w + w t`. -/
    32	theorem sqrt_dual (ell w t : ℝ) (hw : 0 < w) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    33	    2 * ell * Real.sqrt t ≤ ell ^ 2 / w + w * t := by
    34	  have hs : w * t * w = (w * Real.sqrt t) ^ 2 := by
    35	    rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt ht]; ring
    36	  rw [div_add' _ _ _ hw.ne', le_div_iff₀ hw, hs]
    37	  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (ell - w * Real.sqrt t)]
    38	
    39	/-- The identity half of `E:gram-hilbert-square`:
    40	`⟪Φ, z⟫ - ‖Φ‖²/2 = ‖z‖²/2 - ‖Φ - z‖²/2`. -/
    41	theorem hilbert_square_eq {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
    42	    (Φ z : H) :
    43	    inner ℝ Φ z - ‖Φ‖ ^ 2 / 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 - ‖Φ - z‖ ^ 2 / 2 := by
    44	  rw [norm_sub_sq_real]
    45	  ring
    46	
    47	/-- The inequality half of `E:gram-hilbert-square`:
    48	`⟪Φ, z⟫ - ‖Φ‖²/2 ≤ ‖z‖²/2`. -/
    49	theorem hilbert_square_le {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
    50	    (Φ z : H) :
    51	    inner ℝ Φ z - ‖Φ‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 := by
    52	  rw [hilbert_square_eq]
    53	  nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖Φ - z‖]
    54	
    55	/-- `E:gram-hilbert-square` in full: the identity and the inequality. -/
    56	theorem hilbert_square {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
    57	    (Φ z : H) :
    58	    inner ℝ Φ z - ‖Φ‖ ^ 2 / 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 - ‖Φ - z‖ ^ 2 / 2 ∧
    59	      ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 - ‖Φ - z‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 := by
    60	  refine ⟨hilbert_square_eq Φ z, ?_⟩
    61	  nlinarith [sq_nonneg ‖Φ - z‖]
    62	
    63	/-- The finite Gram identity: with `C i j = ⟪k i, k j⟫` (the section's
    64	definition `C_{ij} = \langle k_i,k_j\rangle`), for a finite index set and real
    65	weights, `‖∑ w_i k_i‖² = ∑_{i,j} w_i C_ij w_j`. -/
    66	theorem gram_identity {ι : Type u} {H : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    67	    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
    68	    (k : ι → H) (C : ι → ι → ℝ) (hC : ∀ i j, C i j = inner ℝ (k i) (k j))
    69	    (w : ι → ℝ) :
    70	    ‖∑ i, w i • k i‖ ^ 2 = ∑ i, ∑ j, w i * C i j * w j := by
    71	  rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
    72	  simp only [sum_inner, inner_sum, real_inner_smul_left, real_inner_smul_right, hC]
    73	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
    74	  rw [real_inner_comm (k i) (k j)]
    75	  ring
    76	
    77	/-- `L:gram-scalar-algebra` with the section's own standing hypotheses: a real
    78	Hilbert space (`CompleteSpace H`) and a Gram matrix `C_ij = ⟪k_i, k_j⟫` with
    79	`C_ij ≥ 0` for every pair. These hypotheses are not needed by the proof (see
    80	`sqrt_dual`, `hilbert_square`, `gram_identity`, which hold more generally);
    81	this wrapper states the lemma exactly as the manuscript does. -/
    82	theorem gram_scalar_algebra_paper {ι : Type u} {H : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    83	    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    84	    (k : ι → H) (C : ι → ι → ℝ) (hC : ∀ i j, C i j = inner ℝ (k i) (k j))
    85	    (_hCnn : ∀ i j, 0 ≤ C i j) :
    86	    (∀ ell w t : ℝ, 0 < w → 0 ≤ t → 2 * ell * Real.sqrt t ≤ ell ^ 2 / w + w * t) ∧
    87	      (∀ Φ z : H, inner ℝ Φ z - ‖Φ‖ ^ 2 / 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 - ‖Φ - z‖ ^ 2 / 2 ∧
    88	        ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2 - ‖Φ - z‖ ^ 2 / 2 ≤ ‖z‖ ^ 2 / 2) ∧
    89	      (∀ w : ι → ℝ, ‖∑ i, w i • k i‖ ^ 2 = ∑ i, ∑ j, w i * C i j * w j) :=
    90	  ⟨fun ell w t hw ht => sqrt_dual ell w t hw ht, fun Φ z => hilbert_square Φ z,
    91	    fun w => gram_identity k C hC w⟩
    92	
    93	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.GramScalarAlgebra

    11	module
    12	
    13	public import Mathlib.Tactic

    21	/-- The growth exponent `κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α)` of `E:kappa`. -/
    22	noncomputable def kappa (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) : ℝ := (4 - alpha - alpha0) / (3 - alpha)
    23	
    24	/-- `E:kappa`: under the parameter assumptions of Hypothesis `H:homog`,
    25	`1 < κ < 2`. -/
    26	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3)
    27	    (h0 : 0 < alpha0) (h1 : alpha0 < 1) (hthr : alpha0 + alpha < 2)
    28	    (halpha : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)) :
    29	    kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 := by
    30	  have hd3 : (d : ℝ) ≤ 3 := by
    31	    rcases hd with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
    32	  have h3 : alpha < 3 := by
    33	    rcases halpha with ⟨_, h⟩ | ⟨h, rfl⟩
    34	    · linarith
    35	    · rw [h]; norm_num
    36	  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 3 - alpha := by linarith
    37	  unfold kappa
    38	  constructor
    39	  · rw [lt_div_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
    40	  · rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
    41	
    42	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.KappaRange

     7	`notes/integrated_gaussian_tubes.tex`.
     8	
     9	Manuscript hypotheses made explicit here:
    10	* `G` is defined on all of `ℝ` (Lean convention); the growth bound is assumed
    11	  only on the manuscript domain `r ≥ 0` (the preceding proposition has
    12	  `G : [0, ∞) → ℝ`).  The tail proof uses it only for `r ≥ M`.
    13	* "Borel" is `Measurable G`.
    14	* `δ > 0` (the section fixes `0 < δ < 1`; only `δ > 0` is used).
    15	* Integrability on `(M, ∞)` is part of the conclusion, since the Bochner
    16	  integral of a non-integrable function is `0` in Lean.
    17	-/
    18	public import Mathlib
    19	
    20	@[expose] public section
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	
    26	open MeasureTheory Filter Set Topology
    27	
    28	namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.RayleighTail
    29	
    30	/-- The finite scalar cutoff inequality: for `r ≥ M`,
    31	`C r^ν - r²/2 ≤ -M²/8 - r²/8`. -/
    32	theorem cutoff_split (M r C ν : ℝ)
    33	    (hM : 0 < M) (hr : M ≤ r) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    34	    (_hν1 : 1 < ν) (hν2 : ν < 2) (hcut : 4 * C ≤ M ^ (2 - ν)) :
    35	    C * r ^ ν - r ^ 2 / 2 ≤ -M ^ 2 / 8 - r ^ 2 / 8 := by
    36	  have hrpos : 0 < r := lt_of_lt_of_le hM hr
    37	  have hmono : M ^ (2 - ν) ≤ r ^ (2 - ν) :=
    38	    Real.rpow_le_rpow hM.le hr (by linarith)
    39	  have hs := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hcut.trans hmono)
    40	    (Real.rpow_nonneg hrpos.le ν)
    41	  have hpow : r ^ (2 - ν) * r ^ ν = r ^ 2 := by
    42	    calc
    43	      _ = r ^ ((2 - ν) + ν) := (Real.rpow_add hrpos _ _).symm
    44	      _ = r ^ (2 : ℝ) := by congr 1; ring

    54	theorem gaussian_weight_tail (δ M : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
    55	    IntegrableOn (fun r : ℝ => r / δ * Real.exp (-(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ))) (Ioi M) ∧
    56	      ∫ r in Ioi M, r / δ * Real.exp (-(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) =
    57	        4 * Real.exp (-(M ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) := by
    58	  set F : ℝ → ℝ := fun r => -4 * Real.exp (-(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) with hF

    61	    intro x _

    63	      have := ((hasDerivAt_pow 2 x).neg).div_const (8 * δ)
    64	      simpa using this
    65	    have h2 := (h1.exp).const_mul (-4)
    66	    convert h2 using 1
    67	    field_simp
    68	    ring

    70	    have hq : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => -(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) atTop atBot := by
    71	      have : Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => r ^ 2 / (8 * δ)) atTop atTop :=
    72	        (tendsto_pow_atTop (by norm_num : (2 : ℕ) ≠ 0)).atTop_div_const (by positivity)
    73	      have := tendsto_neg_atTop_atBot.comp this
    74	      refine this.congr (fun r => ?_)
    75	      simp [neg_div]
    76	    have := (Real.tendsto_exp_atBot.comp hq).const_mul (-4)
    77	    simpa [hF] using this
    78	  have hpos : ∀ x ∈ Ioi M, 0 ≤ x / δ * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) := by
    79	    intro x hx
    80	    have hx0 : 0 ≤ x := hM.trans (le_of_lt hx)
    81	    positivity
    82	  have hint := integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonneg' hderiv hpos hlim
    83	  refine ⟨hint, ?_⟩
    84	  rw [integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto' hderiv hint hlim]
    85	  simp [hF]

    87	/-- Lemma `L:tube-rayleigh-tail`, display `E:tube-rayleigh-tail`:
    88	if `G` is Borel, `G r ≤ A₀ + C r^ν` for `r ≥ 0`, `C ≥ 0`, `1 < ν < 2`,
    89	`M > 0` and `4C ≤ M^(2-ν)`, then the integrand is integrable on `(M, ∞)` and
    90	`∫_M^∞ (r/δ) e^{(G(r)-r²/2)/δ} dr ≤ 4 e^{(A₀-M²/4)/δ}`. -/
    91	theorem rayleigh_tail (G : ℝ → ℝ) (hG : Measurable G) (A₀ C ν M δ : ℝ)
    92	    (hgrowth : ∀ r, 0 ≤ r → G r ≤ A₀ + C * r ^ ν)
    93	    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hν1 : 1 < ν) (hν2 : ν < 2) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    94	    (hM : 0 < M) (hcut : 4 * C ≤ M ^ (2 - ν)) :
    95	    IntegrableOn (fun r : ℝ => r / δ * Real.exp ((G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ)) (Ioi M) ∧
    96	      ∫ r in Ioi M, r / δ * Real.exp ((G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ) ≤
    97	        4 * Real.exp ((A₀ - M ^ 2 / 4) / δ) := by
    98	  obtain ⟨hgint, hgval⟩ := gaussian_weight_tail δ M hδ hM.le
    99	  set K : ℝ := Real.exp ((A₀ - M ^ 2 / 8) / δ) with hK
   100	  set g : ℝ → ℝ := fun r => r / δ * Real.exp (-(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ)) with hg
   101	  set f : ℝ → ℝ := fun r => r / δ * Real.exp ((G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ) with hf
   102	  have hfmeas : Measurable f := by
   103	    apply Measurable.mul
   104	    · exact measurable_id.div_const δ
   105	    · exact Real.measurable_exp.comp
   106	        ((hG.sub ((measurable_id.pow_const 2).div_const 2)).div_const δ)
   107	  have hpt : ∀ r ∈ Ioi M, 0 ≤ f r ∧ f r ≤ K * g r := by
   108	    intro r hr
   109	    have hr' : M ≤ r := le_of_lt hr
   110	    have hr0 : 0 < r := hM.trans hr
   111	    have hsplit := cutoff_split M r C ν hM hr' hC hν1 hν2 hcut
   112	    have hGr := hgrowth r hr0.le
   113	    have hexp : (G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ ≤ (A₀ - M ^ 2 / 8) / δ + -(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ) := by
   114	      have : G r - r ^ 2 / 2 ≤ (A₀ - M ^ 2 / 8) + -(r ^ 2) / 8 := by linarith
   115	      calc (G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ ≤ ((A₀ - M ^ 2 / 8) + -(r ^ 2) / 8) / δ :=
   116	            div_le_div_of_nonneg_right this hδ.le
   117	        _ = _ := by field_simp
   118	    have hrd : 0 ≤ r / δ := div_nonneg hr0.le hδ.le
   119	    refine ⟨mul_nonneg hrd (Real.exp_nonneg _), ?_⟩
   120	    have := Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexp
   121	    rw [Real.exp_add] at this

   123	      _ ≤ r / δ * (K * Real.exp (-(r ^ 2) / (8 * δ))) :=
   124	          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left this hrd
   125	      _ = K * g r := by simp only [hg]; ring

   127	  have hfint : IntegrableOn f (Ioi M) := by
   128	    refine Integrable.mono' hKg hfmeas.aestronglyMeasurable ?_
   129	    refine (ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioi).mpr (Eventually.of_forall fun r hr => ?_)
   130	    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (hpt r hr).1]
   131	    exact (hpt r hr).2
   132	  refine ⟨hfint, ?_⟩
   133	  calc ∫ r in Ioi M, f r ≤ ∫ r in Ioi M, K * g r :=
   134	        setIntegral_mono_on hfint hKg measurableSet_Ioi (fun r hr => (hpt r hr).2)
   135	    _ = K * (4 * Real.exp (-(M ^ 2) / (8 * δ))) := by
   136	        rw [integral_const_mul, hgval]
   137	    _ = 4 * Real.exp ((A₀ - M ^ 2 / 4) / δ) := by
   138	        rw [hK, mul_left_comm, ← Real.exp_add]
   139	        congr 2
   140	        field_simp
   141	        ring

   143	/-- The proof's remark "on `[0, M]` the integral is finite as well": under the
   144	growth bound on `r ≥ 0` (here with `C ≥ 0`, `ν > 0` used for monotonicity of
   145	`r ↦ r^ν`), the integrand is integrable on `[0, M]`. -/
   146	theorem rayleigh_head_integrable (G : ℝ → ℝ) (hG : Measurable G) (A₀ C ν M δ : ℝ)
   147	    (hgrowth : ∀ r, 0 ≤ r → G r ≤ A₀ + C * r ^ ν)
   148	    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hν1 : 1 < ν) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hM : 0 < M) :
   149	    IntegrableOn (fun r : ℝ => r / δ * Real.exp ((G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ)) (Icc 0 M) := by
   150	  set f : ℝ → ℝ := fun r => r / δ * Real.exp ((G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ) with hf
   151	  have hfmeas : Measurable f := by
   152	    apply Measurable.mul
   153	    · exact measurable_id.div_const δ
   154	    · exact Real.measurable_exp.comp
   155	        ((hG.sub ((measurable_id.pow_const 2).div_const 2)).div_const δ)
   156	  set B : ℝ := M / δ * Real.exp ((A₀ + C * M ^ ν) / δ)
   157	  refine Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded (M := B) (by simp)
   158	    hfmeas.aestronglyMeasurable ?_
   159	  refine (ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Icc).mpr (Eventually.of_forall fun r hr => ?_)
   160	  obtain ⟨hr0, hrM⟩ := hr
   161	  have hGr := hgrowth r hr0
   162	  have hpow : r ^ ν ≤ M ^ ν := Real.rpow_le_rpow hr0 hrM (by linarith)
   163	  have hsq : 0 ≤ r ^ 2 / 2 := by positivity
   164	  have hexp : (G r - r ^ 2 / 2) / δ ≤ (A₀ + C * M ^ ν) / δ := by
   165	    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hδ.le
   166	    nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hpow hC]
   167	  have hrd : 0 ≤ r / δ := div_nonneg hr0 hδ.le
   168	  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (mul_nonneg hrd (Real.exp_nonneg _))]
   169	  exact mul_le_mul (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hrM hδ.le) (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hexp)
   170	    (Real.exp_nonneg _) (div_nonneg hM.le hδ.le)

   173	section's standing range `0 < δ < 1`: for Borel `G` with

   176	`E:tube-rayleigh-tail`, and it is integrable on `[0, M]`. The lemma's
   177	"In particular" application to another proposition is not formalized. -/
   178	theorem rayleigh_tail_paper (G : ℝ → ℝ) (hG : Measurable G) (A₀ C ν M δ : ℝ)
   179	    (hgrowth : ∀ r, 0 ≤ r → G r ≤ A₀ + C * r ^ ν)
   180	    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hν1 : 1 < ν) (hν2 : ν < 2) (hδ : 0 < δ) (_hδ1 : δ < 1)
   181	    (hM : 0 < M) (hcut : 4 * C ≤ M ^ (2 - ν)) :

     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision ba01d98 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written and reviewed
     8	at the earlier revisions cf979d6 and 669ccc9. The later revisions changed
     9	only prose, titles, the literature review, layout and figures: every cited
    10	label exists in all three, and the mathematical expressions of each cited
    11	statement and its proof are the same up to whitespace and braces (script
    12	checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (101) and the 8 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts. The other 37 public definitions (for example
    22	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    23	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    24	  source or in `Audit/`.
    25	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    26	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    27	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    28	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    29	- The five `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked "whole
    30	  result" below) formalize the conclusions of five labelled results in full,
    31	  in three ways. `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's
    32	  own hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    33	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no
    34	  `delta < 1`) and also stated exactly as the manuscript does by the
    35	  wrappers `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the
    36	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is
    37	  not formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    38	  numerical part of `H:homog` only, a generalization: the covariance part
    39	  of `H:homog` is neither needed nor modelled. Side conditions the TeX
    40	  leaves implicit (a probability measure, integrability, measurability)
    41	  are explicit hypotheses, and integrability is part of each integral
    42	  conclusion.
    43	- The SPDE itself, stochastic integrals, Gaussian measures, Fourier and
    44	  spectral analysis, operator theory and all limits in time or in a
    45	  regularization are outside Lean. Where a Lean statement needs an analytic
    46	  fact about the model, that fact enters as an explicit hypothesis of the
    47	  theorem (a "supplied hypothesis" below). Lean checks the deduction from
    48	  those hypotheses, not the hypotheses themselves.
    49	- A successful `lake build` is not a verification receipt for the
    50	  manuscript. It shows that the stated Lean theorems are proved from their
    51	  hypotheses; whether a statement matches the manuscript step it is listed
    52	  against is a separate, human judgment recorded in this ledger.
    53	- Three further modules developed alongside these (normalized Gaussian
    54	  coordinates, vector Gaussian projection, and colored vector words) are
    55	  withheld from this package because they depend on a library that is not
    56	  yet public.
    57	- "no direct label" means the declaration checks a computation from the
    58	  development of the manuscript that does not appear as, or inside, a
    59	  labeled statement of the revision cited above. Such rows make no claim
    60	  about the manuscript.

   579

   588	  `P:static-phase-all-orders`).

1	\section{Finite Gaussian moments and whole-space Sobolev compactness}
     2	\label{S:compact-gaussian}
     3	
     4	We prove the finite Gaussian and compact-cutoff estimates needed to construct
     5	the wave operator path. All traces and Schatten norms in this section are
     6	unnormalized. The spatial states remain on $\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. Here $p$
     7	is an auxiliary Schatten and Gaussian-moment index. The auxiliary periodic space
     8	below is used only to factor a compactly supported multiplication operator. No
     9	infinite Gaussian series or time path is constructed in this section.
    10	
    11	\subsection{Finite Gaussian matrices with both variance powers}
    12	
    13	\begin{lemma}[Scalar power estimates]\label{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}
    14	  For $0 < \theta < 1$ and $u,v \ge 0$,
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-weighted-power}
    16	    u^\theta v^{1-\theta} \le \theta u+(1-\theta)v.
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  Consequently, if $L > 0$ and $0 \le q \le L$ are integers, then for real
    19	  $x,y$,
    20	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-integer-power}
    21	    |x|^q|y|^{L-q}
    22	    \le \frac qL|x|^L+\frac{L-q}L|y|^L.
    23	  \end{equation}
    24	  For nonnegative finite sequences, the usual H\"older inequality holds with
    25	  exponents $m$ and $m/(m-1)$, $m > 1$. If $Z \ge 0$ has finite expectation $F$
    26	  and $0 < r < 1$, then $\E Z^r \le F^r$.
    27	\end{lemma}
    28	
    29	\begin{proof}
    30	  If $v > 0$, divide~\eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} by $v$ and put $t = u/v$.
    31	  The function $\theta t+1-\theta-t^\theta$ decreases to zero at one and then
    32	  increases, by its derivative $\theta(1-t^{\theta-1})$. Continuity covers $t =
    33	  0$; if $v = 0$ the inequality is immediate. For $0 < q < L$, apply this with
    34	  $u = |x|^L$, $v = |y|^L$ and $\theta = q/L$. The endpoint cases $q = 0,L$ are
    35	  identities, with the ordinary integer convention $a^0 = 1$.
    36	
    37	  To prove finite H\"older, divide the two sequences by their respective
    38	  $\ell^m$ and $\ell^{m/(m-1)}$ norms. If either norm vanishes, the result is
    39	  immediate. Apply~\eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} with $\theta = 1/m$ to the
    40	  corresponding normalized powers and sum; the sum of products is at most one.
    41	  Undo the normalization. Finally, $F = 0$ gives $Z = 0$ almost surely. If $F >
    42	  0$, apply \eqref{E:gaussian-weighted-power} to $u = Z/F$, $v = 1$ and $\theta
    43	  = r$, and integrate. The right side has expectation one. This proves
    44	  Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}.
    45	\end{proof}
    46	
    47	\begin{lemma}[Two Hermitian trace bounds]\label{L:gaussian-trace-bounds}
    48	  Let $B,Y$ be finite Hermitian matrices, $m \ge 2$ an integer, and $L = 2m-2$.
    49	  For integers $0 \le q \le L$,
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-trace-word}
    51	    \operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(BY^qBY^{L-q})
    52	    \le \operatorname{Tr}(B^2|Y|^L).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	  If $D \ge 0$ is Hermitian, then
    55	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gaussian-trace-holder}
    56	    \operatorname{Tr}(D|Y|^{2m-2})
    57	    \le (\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}
    58	    (\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m})^{(m-1)/m}.
    59	  \end{equation}
    60	\end{lemma}
    61	
    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  Diagonalize $Y$, with real eigenvalues $\lambda_i$, and write $b_{ij}$ for the
    64	  entries of $B$ in that basis. Hermitian symmetry gives $b_{ji} =
    65	  \overline{b_{ij}}$. The trace word is the real sum
    66	  \[
    67	    \sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2\lambda_j^q\lambda_i^{L-q}.
    68	  \]
    69	  Bound each product by its absolute value and use
    70	  \eqref{E:gaussian-integer-power}. After interchanging $i,j$, the two resulting
    71	  sums agree because $|b_{ij}| = |b_{ji}|$. Each equals
    72	  $\sum_{i,j}|b_{ij}|^2|\lambda_i|^L = \operatorname{Tr}(B^2|Y|^L)$. The two
    73	  weights sum to one, proving \eqref{E:gaussian-trace-word}. No commutation of
    74	  $B$ and $Y$ is used.
    75	
    76	  In the same basis put $d_i = D_{ii} \ge 0$. If $\theta_j$ are the nonnegative
    77	  eigenvalues of $D$, a unitary change of basis gives $d_i =
    78	  \sum_j|U_{ij}|^2\theta_j$. Both row and column sums of $|U_{ij}|^2$ equal one.
    79	  Finite convexity therefore yields
    80	  \[
    81	    \sum_i d_i^m \le \sum_{i,j}|U_{ij}|^2\theta_j^m
    82	    = \operatorname{Tr}D^m.
    83	  \]
    84	  For completeness, the convexity step follows from $t^m \ge s^m+ms^{m-1}(t-s)$
    85	  for $s,t \ge 0$, obtained by differentiating the difference. Average this
    86	  inequality with $s$ equal to the weighted mean. Now apply finite H\"older from
    87	  Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers} to $\sum_i d_i|\lambda_i|^{2m-2}$. Since
    88	  $(2m-2)m/(m-1) = 2m$, the last display proves \eqref{E:gaussian-trace-holder},
    89	  including zero sums. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-trace-bounds}.
    90	\end{proof}

    92	\begin{proposition}[Finite Gaussian matrix moment]\label{P:finite-gaussian-matrix}
    93	  Let $A_1,\ldots,A_N$ be complex $o$-by-$n$ matrices, with $o,n,N \ge 1$, and
    94	  let $g_k$ be independent real standard Gaussians. Put
    95	  \[
    96	    X=\sum_k g_kA_k,\qquad V_{\rm out}=\sum_k A_kA_k^*,
    97	    \qquad V_{\rm in}=\sum_k A_k^*A_k.
    98	  \]
    99	  For even $p = 2m \ge 2$, with $\|A\|_{S_p}^p = \operatorname{Tr}((A^*A)^m)$,
   100	  \begin{align}
   101	    (\E\|X\|_{S_p}^p)^{1/p}
   102	    &\le \sqrt{p-1}\left(
   103	    \frac{\operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^m+
   104	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^m}{2}\right)^{1/p}
   105	    \label{E:finite-gaussian-average}\\
   106	    &\le \sqrt{p-1}\max\left(
   107	    \|V_{\rm out}^{1/2}\|_{S_p},\|V_{\rm in}^{1/2}\|_{S_p}\right).
   108	    \label{E:finite-gaussian-maximum}
   109	  \end{align}
   110	  The constants are independent of $o,n,N$. The first inequality is an equality
   111	  at $p = 2$. Empty or zero families give the zero identity.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	  First suppose $B_k$ are Hermitian and put $Y = \sum_k g_kB_k$ and $D = \sum_k
   116	  B_k^2$. All polynomial moments are finite because Gaussian decay dominates
   117	  every fixed power. Componentwise integration by parts against the product
   118	  Gaussian density gives $\E[g_kP(g)] = \E[\partial_kP(g)]$, with zero boundary
   119	  terms. It applies to complex polynomials through their real and imaginary
   120	  parts; absolute polynomial integrability justifies Fubini.
   121	
   122	  For $m \ge 2$, put $F = \E\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}$ and $L = 2m-2$. Write
   123	  $\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m} = \sum_k g_k \operatorname{Tr}(B_kY^{2m-1})$ and
   124	  differentiate the $2m-1$ factors in their order. This gives exactly
   125	  \[
   126	    F=\sum_k\sum_{q=0}^{L}
   127	    \E\operatorname{Tr}(B_kY^qB_kY^{L-q}).
   128	  \]
   129	  The eigenbasis calculation above shows these traces are real. The
   130	  differentiated polynomial is real by conjugation and trace cyclicity. No
   131	  derivative of a spectral absolute value or measurable choice of an eigenbasis
   132	  is needed. The two trace bounds give
   133	  \begin{align*}
   134	    F&\le (2m-1)\E\operatorname{Tr}(D|Y|^{2m-2})\\
   135	    &\le (2m-1)(\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}
   136	    \E(\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m})^{(m-1)/m}\\
   137	    &\le (2m-1)(\operatorname{Tr}D^m)^{1/m}F^{(m-1)/m}.
   138	  \end{align*}
   139	  Here $\operatorname{Tr}|Y|^{2m} = \operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}$, and the last
   140	  inequality is the expectation bound in Lemma~\ref{L:gaussian-scalar-powers}.
   141	  If $F = 0$ the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise divide by its positive
   142	  fractional power and raise to $m$ to obtain
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-hermitian-gaussian}
   144	    \E\operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m} \le (2m-1)^m\operatorname{Tr}D^m.
   145	  \end{equation}
   146	  For $m = 1$, independence gives directly $\E\operatorname{Tr}Y^2 =
   147	  \sum_k\operatorname{Tr}B_k^2 = \operatorname{Tr}D$, proving the same formula
   148	  as equality.
   149	
   150	  For rectangular $A_k$, use the Hermitian dilation
   151	  \[
   152	    B_k=\begin{pmatrix}0&A_k\\A_k^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
   153	    Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&X\\X^*&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
   154	    D=\operatorname{diag}(V_{\rm out},V_{\rm in}).
   155	  \]
   156	  Finite entrywise summation proves $\operatorname{Tr}(UV) =
   157	  \operatorname{Tr}(VU)$ for compatible rectangular matrices. Since $(XX^*)^m =
   158	  X(X^*X)^{m-1}X^*$, it follows that
   159	  \[
   160	    \operatorname{Tr}Y^{2m}=2\operatorname{Tr}((X^*X)^m),\qquad
   161	    \operatorname{Tr}D^m=\operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^m+
   162	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^m.
   163	  \]
   164	  Substitute in~\eqref{E:finite-hermitian-gaussian}, divide by two and take the
   165	  $p$th root. This proves~\eqref{E:finite-gaussian-average}. For positive $V$,
   166	  spectral diagonalization gives $\|V^{1/2}\|_{S_p}^p = \operatorname{Tr}V^m$,
   167	  and the average of two nonnegative numbers is bounded by their maximum. At $p
   168	  = 2$, $\E\operatorname{Tr}X^*X = \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in} =
   169	  \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}$, proving the claimed equality. This proves
   170	  Proposition~\ref{P:finite-gaussian-matrix}.
   171	\end{proof}

   173	\begin{remark}[Both variance directions are necessary]
   174	  \label{R:gaussian-one-variance-test}
   175	  Let $n = 16$ and $A_k = e_k^{\mathsf{T}}$ be the coordinate row matrices. The
   176	  only nonzero singular value of $X$ is $(\sum_k g_k^2)^{1/2}$. Gaussian
   177	  integration by parts gives $\E g^2 = 1$, $\E g^4 = 3$, and hence

   179	    \E\|X\|_{S_4}^4=3n+n(n-1)=n(n+2)=288.
   180	  \]

   184	  refutes the corresponding output-only bound. The average and maximum bounds
   185	  have fourth powers $1224$ and $2304$, respectively. This finite example
   186	  asserts nothing about a specialized wave estimate.
   187	\end{remark}

   189	\subsection{Whole-space cutoffs through an auxiliary periodic space}
   190	
   191	Use the unitary Fourier transform with $c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}$ and $\Lambda =
   192	(1-\Delta)^{1/2}$. For real $r$, the norm on $H^r(\R^d)$ is
   193	$\|\langle\xi\rangle^r\widehat{u}\|_2$. The deterministic cutoff arguments allow
   194	any smoothing order $\gamma > 0$. Fix real $\sigma$ and a real compact smooth
   195	$\chi$. Singular values $s_j$, $j \ge 1$, are counted with multiplicity, with
   196	zeros appended when necessary. For compact $K$, put $\|K\|_{S_p}^p = \sum_j
   197	s_j(K)^p$.
   198	
   199	\begin{lemma}[Cutoff factorization]\label{L:cutoff-factorization}
   200	  Choose a cube $Q_L = (-L/2,L/2)^d$ containing $\operatorname{supp}\chi$ in its
   201	  interior, and a real $\psi \in C_c^\infty(Q_L)$ equal to one near
   202	  $\operatorname{supp}\chi$. On the auxiliary torus $\mathbb{T}_L$ use Lebesgue
   203	  measure and the orthonormal basis
   204	  \[
   205	    e_k(x)=L^{-d/2}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x},\qquad
   206	    \kappa_k=2\pi k/L,\qquad k \in \mathbb{Z}^d,
   207	  \]
   208	  with $\|v\|_{H^r(\mathbb{T}_L)}^2 = \sum_k\langle\kappa_k\rangle^{2r}|v_k|^2$.
   209	  Periodization of $\psi u$ and multiplication of a periodic function by $\chi$
   210	  extend to bounded maps
   211	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-periodic-maps}
   212	    \mathcal{P}_\psi:H^r(\R^d)\to H^r(\mathbb{T}_L),\qquad
   213	    \mathcal{E}_\chi:H^r(\mathbb{T}_L)\to H^r(\R^d)
   214	  \end{equation}
   215	  for every real $r$. If $\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ denotes the identity inclusion
   216	  from $H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\mathbb{T}_L)$ to $H^\sigma(\mathbb{T}_L)$, then
   217	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-whole-space-recovery}
   218	    \mathcal{E}_\chi\mathcal{I}_\gamma\mathcal{P}_\psi u=\chi u,
   219	    \qquad u \in H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d).
   220	  \end{equation}
   221	\end{lemma}
   222	
   223	\begin{proof}
   224	  For $x,y \in \R^d$ and real $r$, the elementary inequality $\langle x\rangle
   225	  \le \sqrt{2}\langle y\rangle\langle x-y\rangle$ gives
   226	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-peetre}
   227	    \left(\frac{\langle x\rangle}{\langle y\rangle}\right)^r
   228	    \le 2^{|r|/2}\langle x-y\rangle^{|r|}.
   229	  \end{equation}
   230	  For negative $r$, interchange $x,y$ before raising to $|r|$. Integration by
   231	  parts gives rapid decay of the Fourier transform of every compact smooth
   232	  cutoff. For any lattice spacing $a > 0$ and $N > d$,
   233	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}
   234	    \sup_y\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle y-ak\rangle^{-N}<\infty.
   235	  \end{equation}
   236	  Indeed, translate $y$ into a centered lattice cell, where $|y| \le a\sqrt
   237	  d/2$. For $|k| \ge \sqrt d$ we have $|y-ak| \ge a|k|/2$. The remaining terms
   238	  are finite; the tail converges by dyadic lattice counting, since there are at
   239	  most $C_d2^{jd}$ lattice points in the $j$th shell in $k$. More precisely, for
   240	  $|k| \ge \sqrt d$, the preceding inequality gives
   241	  \[
   242	    \langle y-ak\rangle^{-N}
   243	    \le \max(1,2/a)^N\langle k\rangle^{-N}.
   244	  \]
   245	  The comparison-series terms are bounded by $2^{-jN}$ on each dyadic $k$-shell.
   246	  Thus, its convergent geometric sum carries constants depending on $a,d,N$, as
   247	  does~\eqref{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}.
   248	
   249	  We use the mixed Schur bound for a kernel whose absolute row and column
   250	  integrals are bounded by $M_1,M_2$. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz at each output
   251	  point, followed by Tonelli, bounds its squared operator norm by $M_1M_2$. The
   252	  same proof works with counting measure on one side and Lebesgue measure on the
   253	  other, first on dense finite or compact inputs.
   254	
   255	  For Schwartz $u$, the $k$th coefficient of its cutoff periodization is
   256	  \[
   257	    (\mathcal{P}_\psi u)_k
   258	    = L^{-d/2}\int\psi(x)u(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\ud x
   259	    = L^{-d/2}\int\widehat{\psi}(\kappa_k-\xi)\widehat{u}(\xi)\ud\xi.
   260	  \]
   261	  The $c_d$ from Fourier inversion cancels the $c_d^{-1}$ in the ordinary
   262	  Fourier integral of $\psi$. After weighting, its exact kernel is
   263	  \[
   264	    L^{-d/2}\left(\frac{\langle\kappa_k\rangle}{\langle\xi\rangle}\right)^r
   265	    \widehat{\psi}(\kappa_k-\xi).
   266	  \]
   267	  For a finite torus polynomial $v$, the normalized Fourier kernel of
   268	  $\mathcal{E}_\chi v$ is
   269	  \[
   270	    L^{-d/2}\left(\frac{\langle\xi\rangle}{\langle\kappa_k\rangle}\right)^r
   271	    \widehat{\chi}(\xi-\kappa_k).
   272	  \]
   273	  There is no additional $c_d$ in this kernel. By~\eqref{E:cutoff-peetre}, each
   274	  is bounded in absolute value by a rapidly decreasing function of its frequency
   275	  difference, times a fixed constant. One Schur quantity is its $L^1$ integral
   276	  and the other a uniformly translated lattice sum, bounded
   277	  by~\eqref{E:cutoff-lattice-sum}. This proves~\eqref{E:cutoff-periodic-maps},
   278	  including negative $r$.
   279	
   280	  Smooth compact approximation in weighted Fourier $L^2$ proves Schwartz density
   281	  on $\R^d$; weighted sequence truncation proves polynomial density on the
   282	  torus. Hence, these maps extend uniquely. Their distributional meanings follow
   283	  by testing against compact smooth functions and density: each periodic
   284	  coefficient pairs the distribution with a compact smooth test. No point
   285	  sampling of a rough Fourier function is used. The same full-Lebesgue Schur
   286	  argument proves smooth compact multiplication bounded on every whole-space
   287	  $H^r$.
   288	
   289	  For Schwartz $u$, the periodic Fourier series of $\psi u$ converges smoothly
   290	  on the cube. Since $\chi\psi = \chi$ and $\chi$ is supported strictly inside
   291	  the cube, multiplying this series by $\chi$ recovers $\chi u$ with no alias
   292	  term. Both sides are bounded from $H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d)$ to
   293	  $H^\sigma(\R^d)$, using the just-proved maps, the inclusion and smooth
   294	  multiplication. Density proves \eqref{E:cutoff-whole-space-recovery} on that
   295	  full domain. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization}.
   296	\end{proof}
   297	
   298	\begin{proposition}[Whole-space cutoff singular values]\label{P:cutoff-singular-values}
   299	  For real $\sigma$ and $\gamma > 0$, the initially Schwartz-defined operator
   300	  $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma} = \Lambda^\sigma\chi\Lambda^{-\sigma-\gamma}$ extends
   301	  uniquely to a compact operator on $L^2(\R^d)$, and
   302	  \begin{equation}\label{E:cutoff-singular-values}
   303	    s_j(K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma})
   304	    \le C_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma,d}j^{-\gamma/d},\qquad j \ge 1.
   305	  \end{equation}
   306	  Consequently, $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma} \in S_p$ whenever $p \ge 1$ and $p\gamma
   307	  > d$.
   308	\end{proposition}
   309	
   310	\begin{proof}

311	  The zero cutoff is immediate. Fix one cube and cutoff pair $L,\psi$ as in
   312	  Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization}. Its recovery identity gives
   313	  \[
   314	    K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma}
   315	    =\Lambda^\sigma\mathcal{E}_\chi\mathcal{I}_\gamma
   316	    \mathcal{P}_\psi\Lambda^{-\sigma-\gamma}.
   317	  \]
   318	  In the weighted torus coordinates, $\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ is diagonal with
   319	  entries $\langle\kappa_k\rangle^{-\gamma}$. Let $Q_n$ retain $|k|_\infty \le
   320	  n$. Its rank is $(2n+1)^d$, and
   321	  \[
   322	    \|(1-Q_n)\mathcal{I}_\gamma\|
   323	    \le [1+(2\pi/L)^2(n+1)^2]^{-\gamma/2}\longrightarrow0.
   324	  \]
   325	  Replacing the inclusion by $Q_n\mathcal{I}_\gamma$ gives finite-rank $K_n$
   326	  converging in norm to $K_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma}$. This proves compactness:
   327	  finite-dimensional images have finite nets of each positive radius, and norm
   328	  approximation transfers those nets to the limiting image of the unit ball.
   329	
   330	  Put
   331	  \[
   332	    M=\|\mathcal{E}_\chi:H^\sigma(\mathbb{T}_L)\to H^\sigma(\R^d)\|
   333	    \|\mathcal{P}_\psi:H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\R^d)
   334	    \to H^{\sigma+\gamma}(\mathbb{T}_L)\|.
   335	  \]
   336	  The outer Bessel maps are unitary. For $j \ge 3^d$, choose $n = \lfloor
   337	  j^{1/d}/4\rfloor$. Then
   338	  \[
   339	    (2n+1)^d\le(j^{1/d}/2+1)^d<j,\qquad
   340	    \|K-K_n\|\le M(2L/\pi)^\gamma j^{-\gamma/d}.
   341	  \]
   342	  The second estimate follows from $n+1 > j^{1/d}/4$. For a compact operator,
   343	  every rank less than $j$ approximation $F$ satisfies $s_j(K) \le \|K-F\|$: the
   344	  span of the first $j$ right singular vectors contains a unit vector in $\ker
   345	  F$, on which $\|K\cdot\| \ge s_j(K)$. If $s_j(K) = 0$ the inequality is
   346	  immediate. For $j < 3^d$ use $s_j(K) \le \|K\| \le M$. Thus, one may take
   347	  \[
   348	    C_{\chi,\sigma,\gamma,d}
   349	    =M\max(3^\gamma,(2L/\pi)^\gamma).
   350	  \]
   351	  Finally, $\sum_j j^{-p\gamma/d}$ converges for $p\gamma > d$. This proves
   352	  Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values}.
   353	\end{proof}
   354	
   355	No uniform support-radius constant or endpoint necessity is asserted in
   356	Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values}. The periodic inclusion was only a
   357	factor of the recovered whole-space operator.

   359	\subsection{Balanced adjoints and localized variance envelopes}
   360	
   361	For $E = H^{1/2}(\R^d)\times H^{-1/2}(\R^d)$ use the physical unitary
   362	coordinates
   363	\[
   364	  J_0(u,v)=(\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v),\qquad
   365	  H=L^2(\R^d;\mathbb{C}^2).
   366	\]
   367	The frequency map $J$ in Section~\ref{S:wave-variance} is
   368	$(\mathcal{F}\oplus\mathcal{F})J_0$. Let $D_\chi$ multiply both phase entries
   369	and define
   370	\begin{align}
   371	  P_\chi&=J_0D_\chi J_0^{-1},\qquad
   372	  D_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda^{-\gamma},\Lambda^{-\gamma}),
   373	  \label{E:compact-balanced-cutoff}\\
   374	  K_{\rm out}&=P_\chi D_\gamma,\qquad
   375	  K_{\rm in}=P_\chi^*D_\gamma.
   376	  \label{E:compact-two-factors}
   377	\end{align}
   378	
   379	\begin{proposition}[Both compact envelopes]\label{P:compact-two-envelopes}
   380	  The operator $P_\chi$ is bounded. For the unitary swap $U(v,w) = (w,v)$,
   381	  \[
   382	    P_\chi^*=UP_\chi U,\qquad K_{\rm in}=UK_{\rm out}U.
   383	  \]
   384	  Both factors are compact and have equal $S_p$ norms for $p \ge 1$, $p\gamma >
   385	  d$. For $p \ge 2$, $p\gamma > d$, the positive compact operators
   386	  \[
   387	    B_{\rm out}=P_\chi D_\gamma^2P_\chi^*=K_{\rm out}K_{\rm out}^*,
   388	    \qquad B_{\rm in}=P_\chi^*D_\gamma^2P_\chi=K_{\rm in}K_{\rm in}^*
   389	  \]
   390	  satisfy
   391	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-envelope-traces}
   392	    \operatorname{Tr}B_{\rm out}^{p/2}
   393	    =\operatorname{Tr}B_{\rm in}^{p/2}=\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   394	  \end{equation}
   395	\end{proposition}
   396	
   397	\begin{proof}
   398	  Put $A_\sigma = \Lambda^\sigma\chi\Lambda^{-\sigma}$. The full-Lebesgue Schur
   399	  argument in Lemma~\ref{L:cutoff-factorization} shows boundedness for every
   400	  real $\sigma$. On Schwartz functions, self-adjointness of real multiplication
   401	  and of the Bessel powers gives $A_\sigma^* = A_{-\sigma}$. Density and
   402	  boundedness extend this to the Hilbert adjoints. No evenness of $\chi$ is
   403	  needed. Thus,
   404	  \[
   405	    P_\chi=\operatorname{diag}(A_{1/2},A_{-1/2}),\qquad
   406	    P_\chi^*=\operatorname{diag}(A_{-1/2},A_{1/2})=UP_\chi U.
   407	  \]
   408	  The swap commutes with $D_\gamma$, giving the claimed factor identity. The
   409	  blocks of $K_{\rm out}$ are $K_{\chi,1/2,\gamma}$ and $K_{\chi,-1/2,\gamma}$.
   410	  Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-singular-values} gives compactness and $S_p$
   411	  membership. The singular values of their direct sum form the multiset union,
   412	  so
   413	  \[
   414	    \|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p
   415	    =\|K_{\chi,1/2,\gamma}\|_{S_p}^p+
   416	    \|K_{\chi,-1/2,\gamma}\|_{S_p}^p.
   417	  \]
   418	  Unitary conjugation preserves them. Finally, the positive eigenvalues of
   419	  $KK^*$ and $K^*K$ agree with multiplicity: on an eigenspace with eigenvalue
   420	  $\lambda > 0$, the maps $K/\sqrt\lambda$ and $K^*/\sqrt\lambda$ are inverse
   421	  isometries. Zero eigenvalues contribute nothing to the trace. Summing these
   422	  scalar powers proves~\eqref{E:compact-envelope-traces}. This proves
   423	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-two-envelopes}.
   424	\end{proof}
   425	
   426	We use the usual positive square root of a bounded positive operator and the
   427	spectral decomposition of compact positive operators. The needed order argument
   428	is recorded explicitly.
   429	
   430	\begin{lemma}[Compact positive order and trace]\label{L:compact-positive-order}
   431	  If $A,B$ are bounded self-adjoint operators with $0 \le A \le B$ and $B$
   432	  compact positive, then $A$ is compact and its ordered eigenvalues satisfy
   433	  $\lambda_j(A) \le \lambda_j(B)$, including zero padding. Consequently, for $t
   434	  \ge 1$ with finite $\operatorname{Tr}B^t$,
   435	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-trace}
   436	    \operatorname{Tr}A^t\le\operatorname{Tr}B^t.
   437	  \end{equation}
   438	\end{lemma}
   439	
   440	\begin{proof}
   441	  Let $Q_n$ be finite spectral projections of $B$ whose tails tend to zero in
   442	  norm. Then
   443	  \[
   444	    \|(1-Q_n)A^{1/2}\|^2
   445	    =\|(1-Q_n)A(1-Q_n)\|
   446	    \le\|(1-Q_n)B(1-Q_n)\|\longrightarrow0.
   447	  \]
   448	  Thus, $A^{1/2}$ is a norm limit of finite-rank operators and is compact, as is
   449	  $A$. For compact positive operators, the max-min formula for $\lambda_j$
   450	  follows in an eigenbasis: the span of the first $j$ eigenvectors gives the
   451	  lower bound for the supremum over $j$-dimensional subspaces of their minimum
   452	  Rayleigh quotient, while every such subspace meets the orthogonal complement
   453	  of the first $j-1$ eigenvectors, giving the upper bound. Compare the Rayleigh
   454	  quotients of $A$ and $B$ to obtain the eigenvalue inequality. Sum the ordered
   455	  scalar powers to prove \eqref{E:compact-positive-trace}. No inequality $A^t
   456	  \le B^t$ is asserted. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:compact-positive-order}.
   457	\end{proof}
   458	
   459	\begin{proposition}[Localized finite variance bounds]\label{P:localized-finite-variance}
   460	  Suppose finitely many bounded operators $Z_\ell$ on $H$ satisfy
   461	  \begin{equation}\label{E:localized-finite-hypotheses}
   462	    P_\chi Z_\ell=Z_\ell=Z_\ell P_\chi,\qquad
   463	    V_{\rm out}:=\sum_\ell Z_\ell Z_\ell^*\le CD_\gamma^2,\qquad
   464	    V_{\rm in}:=\sum_\ell Z_\ell^*Z_\ell\le CD_\gamma^2,
   465	  \end{equation}
   466	  with $C \ge 0$. If $p \ge 2$ and $p\gamma > d$, every $Z_\ell$ is compact in
   467	  $S_p$, the two variances are compact in $S_{p/2}$, and
   468	  \begin{align}
   469	    V_{\rm out}&\le CB_{\rm out},\qquad V_{\rm in}\le CB_{\rm in},
   470	    \label{E:localized-two-envelopes}\\
   471	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^{p/2},\quad
   472	    \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm in}^{p/2}
   473	    &\le C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   474	    \label{E:localized-trace-bounds}
   475	  \end{align}
   476	\end{proposition}
   477	
   478	\begin{proof}
   479	  Left localization gives $V_{\rm out} = P_\chi V_{\rm out}P_\chi^*$. Apply
   480	  positive congruence to the output bound
   481	  in~\eqref{E:localized-finite-hypotheses} to get $V_{\rm out} \le CP_\chi
   482	  D_\gamma^2P_\chi^* = CB_{\rm out}$. Right localization similarly gives $V_{\rm
   483	  in} = P_\chi^*V_{\rm in}P_\chi \le CB_{\rm in}$.
   484	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-two-envelopes} and
   485	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-positive-order} prove compactness and the two trace
   486	  bounds with $t = p/2$. If $C = 0$, both variances and every $Z_\ell$ vanish,
   487	  so all assertions are immediate.
   488	
   489	  For each $\ell$, $Z_\ell Z_\ell^* \le V_{\rm out}$ is compact by the same
   490	  lemma. Its finite spectral projections $Q_n$ give $\|(1-Q_n)Z_\ell\|^2 =
   491	  \|(1-Q_n)Z_\ell Z_\ell^*(1-Q_n)\| \to 0$. Hence, $Z_\ell$ is compact. Its
   492	  singular values squared are the nonzero eigenvalues of $Z_\ell Z_\ell^*$.
   493	  Comparing with $V_{\rm out}$ and summing proves $Z_\ell \in S_p$ with
   494	  $\|Z_\ell\|_{S_p}^p \le \operatorname{Tr}V_{\rm out}^{p/2}$. This proves
   495	  Proposition~\ref{P:localized-finite-variance}.
   496	\end{proof}
   497	
   498	The two localization identities are hypotheses here; a noise coefficient family
   499	has not yet been shown to satisfy them. In particular, $P_\chi$ is not assumed
   500	self-adjoint or a projection.
   501	
   502	\begin{corollary}[Finite Gaussian operators]\label{C:finite-gaussian-operators}
   503	  Under~\eqref{E:localized-finite-hypotheses}, let $g_\ell$ be independent real
   504	  standard Gaussians. For even $p \ge 2$ with $p\gamma > d$, the finite sum $X =
   505	  \sum_\ell g_\ell Z_\ell$ satisfies
   506	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gaussian-operator-bound}
   507	    (\E\|X\|_{S_p}^p)^{1/p}
   508	    \le\sqrt{p-1}\sqrt C\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}.
   509	  \end{equation}
   510	  Its extended norm is measurable, with finite expectation as displayed.
   511	\end{corollary}
   512	
   513	\begin{proof}
   514	  Choose finite-rank orthogonal projections $\Pi_n$ from a countable orthonormal
   515	  basis of $H$, with $\Pi_n \to I$ strongly. Put $Z_{\ell,n} = \Pi_nZ_\ell\Pi_n$
   516	  and $X_n = \sum_\ell g_\ell Z_{\ell,n}$, viewed as matrices on
   517	  $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_n$. Their output variance satisfies
   518	  \[
   519	    \sum_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell^*\Pi_n
   520	    \le\Pi_nV_{\rm out}\Pi_n,
   521	  \]
   522	  since the difference is $\sum_\ell\Pi_nZ_\ell(1-\Pi_n)Z_\ell^*\Pi_n \ge 0$.
   523	  The input inequality is identical with adjoints interchanged. Compact max-min
   524	  also gives $\lambda_j(\Pi_nV\Pi_n) \le \lambda_j(V)$ for positive compact $V$,
   525	  since Rayleigh subspaces inside $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_n$ form a subset of all
   526	  subspaces. Thus, both variance trace powers of these matrices are bounded by
   527	  $C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p$.
   528	
   529	  Proposition~\ref{P:finite-gaussian-matrix} applies to these finite complex
   530	  matrices, the same real independent Gaussians and the even $p$. Taking the
   531	  average of the two already bounded trace powers gives
   532	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gaussian-compression-bound}
   533	    \E\|X_n\|_{S_p}^p
   534	    \le(p-1)^{p/2}C^{p/2}\|K_{\rm out}\|_{S_p}^p.
   535	  \end{equation}
   536	  No factor two is added by this average.
   537	
   538	  For each Gaussian coordinate vector, $X$ is a finite sum of compact operators.
   539	  Strong convergence of $\Pi_n$ implies $\Pi_nX\Pi_n \to X$ in operator norm:
   540	  approximate $X$ by a finite-rank $F$, use uniform strong convergence on the
   541	  finite-dimensional ranges of $F$ and $F^*$, and control the remainder using
   542	  $\|\Pi_n\| \le 1$. Singular values are norm-Lipschitz. Indeed, their formula
   543	  \[
   544	    s_j(A)=\inf_{\dim L<j}
   545	    \sup_{v\in L^\perp,\ \|v\|=1}\|Av\|
   546	  \]
   547	  follows from compact singular vectors and gives $s_j(A) \le s_j(B)+\|A-B\|$,
   548	  and the reverse bound by interchanging $A,B$. Hence, $s_j(X_n) \to s_j(X)$ for
   549	  each $j$. Fatou for the nonnegative singular-value sum gives $\|X\|_{S_p}^p
   550	  \le \liminf_n\|X_n\|_{S_p}^p$, allowing extended infinity. These variables are
   551	  measurable: the finite Gaussian coordinate map into operators is
   552	  norm-continuous, each singular value is continuous, and the norm power is
   553	  their nonnegative measurable sum. Fatou in probability
   554	  and~\eqref{E:finite-gaussian-compression-bound} prove the bound and
   555	  almost-sure finiteness. No $S_p$-Bochner convergence is assumed. This proves
   556	  Corollary~\ref{C:finite-gaussian-operators}.
   557	\end{proof}

   559	\subsection{A nonzero witness and the need for a compact cutoff}
   560	
   561	\begin{proposition}[Whole-space cutoff tests]\label{P:cutoff-boundary-tests}
   562	  If $\chi$ equals one on a nonempty open set, there is a nonzero rank-one
   563	  operator satisfying~\eqref{E:localized-finite-hypotheses} with a finite common
   564	  $C$. On the other hand, $\Lambda^{-\gamma}$ on $L^2(\R^d)$ is not compact for
   565	  any $\gamma > 0$.
   566	\end{proposition}
   567	
   568	\begin{proof}
   569	  Choose nonzero real $v,f \in C_c^\infty$ supported inside the plateau, and put
   570	  $\widetilde{v} = (\Lambda^{1/2}v,0)$ and $\widetilde{w} =
   571	  (\Lambda^{-1/2}f,0)$. Both are Schwartz. The block formulas give
   572	  $P_\chi\widetilde{v} = \widetilde{v}$ and $P_\chi^*\widetilde{w} =
   573	  \widetilde{w}$. Therefore, $Zx = \langle x,\widetilde{w}\rangle\widetilde{v}$
   574	  satisfies $P_\chi Z = Z = ZP_\chi$. Its two variances are
   575	  $\|\widetilde{w}\|^2\widetilde{v}\otimes\widetilde{v}^*$ and
   576	  $\|\widetilde{v}\|^2\widetilde{w}\otimes\widetilde{w}^*$. For any Schwartz $a$
   577	  and any $x \in H$,
   578	  \[
   579	    |\langle x,a\rangle|
   580	    =|\langle D_\gamma x,D_\gamma^{-1}a\rangle|
   581	    \le\|D_\gamma x\|\|D_\gamma^{-1}a\|.
   582	  \]
   583	  The inverse multiplier is applied only to Schwartz $a$, so it belongs to $H$.
   584	  Apply the inequality with $a = \widetilde{v},\widetilde{w}$ to obtain the two
   585	  variance bounds with
   586	  \[
   587	    C=\max\left(
   588	    \|\widetilde{w}\|^2\|D_\gamma^{-1}\widetilde{v}\|^2,
   589	    \|\widetilde{v}\|^2\|D_\gamma^{-1}\widetilde{w}\|^2\right)<\infty.
   590	  \]
   591	  This witness uses a plateau; no nonzero family is inferred for every compact
   592	  cutoff or identified with a source family.
   593	
   594	  For noncompactness, take $f$ with nonzero Gaussian Fourier transform. Then $g
   595	  = \Lambda^{-\gamma}f$ is a nonzero Schwartz function. The images of translates
   596	  of $f$ are the same translates of $g$. With $T_hg(x) = g(x-h)$, Plancherel
   597	  gives
   598	  \[
   599	    \langle T_hg,g\rangle
   600	    =\int e^{-i\xi\cdot h}|\widehat{g}(\xi)|^2\ud\xi
   601	    =c_d^{-1}\widehat{|\widehat{g}|^2}(h).
   602	  \]
   603	  This tends to zero because $|\widehat{g}|^2$ is Schwartz. Choose a large
   604	  spacing so that any two distinct translates in the resulting sequence have
   605	  image distance at least $\|g\|$. The input norms are identical, but the images
   606	  have no Cauchy subsequence. This disproves compactness. This proves
   607	  Proposition~\ref{P:cutoff-boundary-tests}.
   608	\end{proof}
   609	
   610	Thus, the choice $\chi = 1$ cannot be substituted into the compact-cutoff
   611	argument. No necessity at the Schatten endpoint $p\gamma = d$ is asserted. The
   612	results concern finite matrices and conditional finite operator sums.
   613	Coefficient localization, compact variance tails, an infinite Gaussian series
   614	and time regularity are proved in Section~\ref{S:actual-operator-driver}; source
   615	and Young identification are proved in
   616	Sections~\ref{S:source-driver-convergence}--\ref{S:constant-phase-young}. They
   617	are not consequences of the finite comparison alone.
     1	\section{Finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries}
     2	\label{S:finite-positive-gram}
     3	
     4	Let $H$ be any real Hilbert space, $\mathcal{I}$ a finite index set, $k_i \in
     5	H$, $\ell_i > 0$ and $b_i \ge 0$. Write $C_{ij} = \langle k_i,k_j\rangle$ and
     6	assume $C_{ij} \ge 0$ for every pair. The Gram matrix is symmetric and positive
     7	semidefinite, since $\sum_{i,j}a_iC_{ij}a_j = \|\sum_i a_i k_i\|^2$. Put $t_+ =
     8	\max(t,0)$ and define
     9	\begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gram-score}
    10	  \mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi)
    11	  =2\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\ell_i
    12	  \sqrt{(\langle\Phi,k_i\rangle-b_i)_+}-\|\Phi\|^2/2,
    13	  \qquad \mathscr{S}(C)=\sup_{\Phi\in H}\mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi).
    14	\end{equation}
    15	Let $\mathcal{J} = \{i:k_i\ne0\} = \{i:C_{ii}>0\}$. Zero vectors contribute zero
    16	because $b_i \ge 0$. Empty index sets, singular Grams and $H = \{0\}$ are
    17	allowed. For nonempty $A \subset \mathcal{J}$ and $w_i > 0$, set
    18	\begin{equation}\label{E:finite-gram-dual}
    19	  D_A^C(w)=\sum_{i\in A}\frac{\ell_i^2}{w_i}
    20	  -\sum_{i\in A}b_iw_i
    21	  +\frac12\sum_{i,j\in A}w_iC_{ij}w_j,
    22	  \qquad d_A^C=\inf_{w_i>0}D_A^C(w).
    23	\end{equation}
    24	Set $d_\varnothing^C = 0$.
    25	
    26	\begin{lemma}[Scalar and Hilbert identities]\label{L:gram-scalar-algebra}
    27	  For real $\ell$, $w > 0$ and $t \ge 0$,
    28	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gram-sqrt-dual}
    29	    2\ell\sqrt t\le\ell^2/w+wt.
    30	  \end{equation}
    31	  For $\Phi,z \in H$,
    32	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gram-hilbert-square}
    33	    \langle\Phi,z\rangle-\|\Phi\|^2/2
    34	    =\|z\|^2/2-\|\Phi-z\|^2/2\le\|z\|^2/2.
    35	  \end{equation}
    36	  For finite real $w_i$, $\|\sum_iw_ik_i\|^2 = \sum_{i,j}w_iC_{ij}w_j$.
    37	\end{lemma}
    38	
    39	\begin{proof}
    40	  Since $\sqrt w > 0$ and $\sqrt{wt} = \sqrt w\sqrt t$,
    41	  \[
    42	    0\le(\ell/\sqrt w-\sqrt{wt})^2
    43	    =\ell^2/w+wt-2\ell\sqrt t.
    44	  \]
    45	  This includes $t = 0$. If $\ell,t > 0$, equality holds for $w = \ell/\sqrt t$.
    46	  Expanding $\|\Phi-z\|^2$ proves~\eqref{E:gram-hilbert-square}. Bilinearity of
    47	  the real inner product proves the finite Gram identity. These identities use
    48	  neither compactness of a Hilbert ball nor an inverse covariance matrix. This
    49	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:gram-scalar-algebra}.
    50	\end{proof}
    51	
    52	\begin{lemma}[Interior dual minimum]\label{L:gram-dual-minimum}
    53	  Each nonempty $A \subset \mathcal{J}$ has a unique positive minimizer $w^A$ of
    54	  $D_A^C$. At this minimizer,
    55	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gram-dual-stationarity}
    56	    \sum_{j\in A}C_{ij}w_j^A-b_i
    57	    =\frac{\ell_i^2}{(w_i^A)^2}>0,\qquad i\in A.
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	\end{lemma}
    60	
    61	\begin{proof}
    62	  Put $c_i = C_{ii} > 0$ and $K_A = \sum_{i\in A}b_i^2/c_i$. Nonnegative entries
    63	  and positive weights give
    64	  \[
    65	    D_A^C(w)\ge
    66	    \sum_i\left(\ell_i^2/w_i-b_iw_i+c_iw_i^2/2\right).
    67	  \]
    68	  Completing the square in $c_iw_i^2/4-b_iw_i$ yields
    69	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gram-dual-coercivity}
    70	    D_A^C(w)\ge
    71	    \sum_i\ell_i^2/w_i+\frac14\sum_i c_iw_i^2-K_A.
    72	  \end{equation}
    73	  Thus, no coordinate can approach zero or infinity in a bounded sublevel while
    74	  a different negative term hides its growth. Take $w^0 = (1,\ldots,1)$, $d_0 =
    75	  D_A^C(w^0)$ and $L_A = d_0+K_A$. Equation~\eqref{E:gram-dual-coercivity} at
    76	  $w^0$ gives $L_A \ge \sum_i\ell_i^2+\sum_i c_i/4 > 0$. Every $w$ with
    77	  $D_A^C(w) \le d_0$ satisfies
    78	  \[
    79	    \ell_i^2/L_A\le w_i\le\sqrt{4L_A/c_i}.
    80	  \]
    81	  The sublevel is nonempty and closed inside this compact box, which lies in the
    82	  open positive orthant. A minimizing sequence chosen in the sublevel has a
    83	  convergent subsequence there. Continuity attains its infimum. Outside this
    84	  sublevel the values exceed $d_0$, so the minimum is global on the entire
    85	  positive orthant.
    86	
    87	  The function is smooth in that orthant. Its Hessian on a nonzero vector $\xi$
    88	  has value
    89	  \[
    90	    \sum_i\frac{2\ell_i^2}{w_i^3}\xi_i^2
    91	    +\sum_{i,j}\xi_iC_{ij}\xi_j>0.
    92	  \]
    93	  The first term is strictly positive and the second is a squared Hilbert norm.
    94	  Restriction to any nonconstant line segment is strictly convex, proving
    95	  uniqueness. Each coordinate permits both signs of a small perturbation at the
    96	  interior minimum. Differentiation gives $-\ell_i^2/w_i^2-b_i+\sum_jC_{ij}w_j =
    97	  0$. This is~\eqref{E:gram-dual-stationarity}. This proves
    98	  Lemma~\ref{L:gram-dual-minimum}.
    99	\end{proof}
   100	
   101	\begin{proposition}[Positive conic maximizer]\label{P:gram-positive-optimizer}
   102	  The finite real value in~\eqref{E:finite-gram-score} satisfies
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:gram-active-duality}
   104	    \mathscr{S}(C)=\max_{A\subset\mathcal{J}}d_A^C .
   105	  \end{equation}
   106	  If a maximizing subset is empty, $\Phi = 0$ attains the supremum. If a
   107	  maximizing subset $A$ is nonempty, a maximizer is $\Phi_A = \sum_{i\in A}w_i^A
   108	  k_i$ with strictly positive coefficients. No uniqueness of the primal
   109	  maximizer or maximizing subset is asserted.
   110	\end{proposition}
   111	
   112	\begin{proof}
   113	  For arbitrary $\Phi$, let $A(\Phi) = \{i:\langle\Phi,k_i\rangle>b_i\}$. It is
   114	  contained in $\mathcal{J}$. All other terms in the objective vanish, including
   115	  equality at the threshold. If $A(\Phi)$ is empty, $\mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi) =
   116	  -\|\Phi\|^2/2 \le 0$. Otherwise, for any positive $w$ on $A = A(\Phi)$, set
   117	  $t_i = \langle\Phi,k_i\rangle-b_i > 0$ and $z = \sum_{i\in A}w_ik_i$.
   118	  Lemma~\ref{L:gram-scalar-algebra} gives
   119	  \[
   120	    \mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi)
   121	    \le\sum_i\ell_i^2/w_i-\sum_i b_iw_i
   122	    +\langle\Phi,z\rangle-\|\Phi\|^2/2
   123	    \le D_A^C(w).
   124	  \]
   125	  This holds for every positive $w$, so $\mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi) \le d_A^C$. There
   126	  are finitely many subsets and their values are finite by
   127	  Lemma~\ref{L:gram-dual-minimum}. Taking the supremum bounds $\mathscr{S}(C)$
   128	  above by their maximum.
   129	
   130	  Conversely, $\mathfrak{F}_C(0) = 0 = d_\varnothing^C$. For nonempty $A$, take
   131	  its dual minimizer. Equation~\eqref{E:gram-dual-stationarity} makes every
   132	  vector in $A$ strictly active at $\Phi_A$, with
   133	  $\sqrt{\langle\Phi_A,k_i\rangle-b_i} = \ell_i/w_i^A$. Both inequalities in the
   134	  preceding display are then equalities for the sum restricted to $A$, since $z
   135	  = \Phi_A$. This restricted objective equals $d_A^C$. All omitted vectors
   136	  contribute nonnegative terms to the full objective, hence
   137	  $\mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi_A) \ge d_A^C$, even if this value is negative. Maximizing
   138	  over $A$, including the empty set, proves \eqref{E:gram-active-duality} and
   139	  the asserted attainment. For a maximizing nonempty subset the upper and lower
   140	  bounds force $\mathfrak{F}_C(\Phi_A) = d_A^C$; no outside inactivity was
   141	  assumed. All-zero vectors give $\mathscr{S}(C) = 0$ directly. This proves
   142	  Proposition~\ref{P:gram-positive-optimizer}.
   143	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{lemma}[Real Gram realization]\label{L:gram-realization}
   150	  Every finite real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix is the Gram matrix of
   151	  vectors in a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space. When its entries are
   152	  nonnegative, the value $\mathscr{S}(C)$ is independent of its realization.
   153	\end{lemma}
   154	
   155	\begin{proof}
   156	  Induct on the size, with the empty matrix realized in $\{0\}$. Diagonal
   157	  entries are nonnegative. If all vanish, testing on $e_i+t e_j$ gives $2tC_{ij}
   158	  \ge 0$ for every real $t$, hence $C = 0$, realized by zero vectors. Otherwise
   159	  permute a positive diagonal $c$ into the first position and write $C =
   160	  \left[\begin{smallmatrix}c&v^{\mathsf{T}}\\v&A\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The
   161	  Schur complement $B = A-vv^{\mathsf{T}}/c$ is positive semidefinite: test the
   162	  original quadratic form on $(-v^{\mathsf{T}}y/c,y)$. Realize $B$ by vectors
   163	  $u_i$ using the induction hypothesis. Then $k_1 = (\sqrt c,0)$ and $k_i =
   164	  (v_i/\sqrt c,u_i)$ for the other indices realize $C$. Undo the permutation.
   165	  Entries of $B$ need not be nonnegative; this construction requires neither
   166	  nonnegative coordinates nor complete positivity.
   167	
   168	  In any realization, $C_{ii} = 0$ means $k_i = 0$, so its entire row vanishes.
   169	  Formula~\eqref{E:gram-active-duality} depends only on $C,\ell,b$ and these
   170	  eligible indices. It therefore proves realization independence whenever the
   171	  entries are nonnegative, which is the scope in which $\mathscr{S}(C)$ is used.
   172	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:gram-realization}.
   173	\end{proof}
   174	
   175	\begin{proposition}[Entrywise Gram comparison]\label{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}
   176	  Let $C,D$ be real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices on the same finite
   177	  index set, with $0 \le C_{ij} \le D_{ij}$. With the same $\ell_i > 0,b_i \ge
   178	  0$,
   179	  \[
   180	    \mathscr{S}(C)\le\mathscr{S}(D).
   181	  \]
   182	  No positive-semidefinite order on $D-C$ is required.
   183	\end{proposition}
   184	
   185	\begin{proof}
   186	  Lemma~\ref{L:gram-realization} defines both values. Their eligible sets
   187	  satisfy $\mathcal{J}_C \subset \mathcal{J}_D$. For nonempty $A \subset
   188	  \mathcal{J}_C$ and positive weights,
   189	  \[
   190	    D_A^D(w)-D_A^C(w)
   191	    =\frac12\sum_{i,j\in A}w_i(D_{ij}-C_{ij})w_j\ge0.
   192	  \]
   193	  Taking infima gives $d_A^C \le d_A^D$. The empty values are both zero. Taking
   194	  maxima and using the inclusion of eligible families proves the claim by
   195	  Proposition~\ref{P:gram-positive-optimizer}. This includes the appearance of
   196	  previously zero vectors. This proves
   197	  Proposition~\ref{P:gram-entrywise-comparison}.
   198	\end{proof}
   199	
   200	\begin{remark}[Exact checks and scope]\label{R:gram-controls}
   201	  The empty value is essential: for one vector with $C = 1$, $\ell = 1/10,b =
   202	  4$, the nonempty dual has $D(4) = -3199/400 < 0$, whereas the primal objective
   203	  at zero is zero. Global concavity is unavailable: for $k = \ell = b = 1$ the
   204	  objective $2\sqrt{(\phi-1)_+}-\phi^2/2$ decreases on $[0,1]$ and has infinite
   205	  positive right slope at one. For $k = \ell = 1,b = 0$, differentiation on
   206	  $\phi > 0$ gives the maximum $3/2$ at $\phi = 1$; on $\phi \le 0$ the
   207	  objective is nonpositive. Doubling the cost changes the positive critical
   208	  point to $2^{-2/3}$ and the maximum to $3\,2^{-4/3}$. Finally, $C = I_2$, $D =
   209	  \left[\begin{smallmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ are nonnegative
   210	  positive semidefinite Grams but $D-C$ has eigenvalues $1/2,-1/2$. These are
   211	  finite analytic checks, not a covariance-order theorem for physical waves.
   212	
   213	  The scalar, finite Gram, conditional active upper and half-quadratic entrywise
   214	  deductions have existing local Lean certificates at their exact hypotheses.
   215	  Dual coercivity, calculus, attainment, realization and the infimum/maximum
   216	  argument above remain analytic proofs. No new kernel fact or formalization of
   217	  the physical application follows merely from these certificates.
   218	\end{remark}

1	\section{The Gaussian operator path}
     2	\label{S:actual-operator-driver}
     3	
     4	We now construct the integrated operator path in the interaction representation
     5	on the same probability space as the original noise. Retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, set $a = \alpha_0$, $s = 1/2$ and $E_r =
     7	H^r(\R^d)\times H^{r-1}(\R^d)$, and initially use real phases $E = E_s$. Let
     8	$H_W$ be the real completion of $C_c^\infty((0,\infty)\times\R^d)$ modulo its
     9	covariance-null tests. The given isonormal process on it is $W$. If $\Gamma =
    10	0$, the operator path and all covariance forms are zero, so the conclusions
    11	below hold directly. Assume $\Gamma \ne 0$ in the construction.
    12	
    13	Choose and fix $R,T > 0$ and a real even nonnegative $\zeta \in
    14	C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ equal to one on $B_1$ and zero off $B_2$. The physical mask is
    15	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$. The free group $S(t)$ and forms $\ell_R$ are those of
    16	Section~\ref{S:wave-variance}; both phase entries and the continuous
    17	zero-frequency sine quotient are retained. Fix parameters
    18	\begin{equation}\label{E:driver-parameters}
    19	  0<\gamma<\min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right),\qquad
    20	  \frac12<\theta<\beta<\min\left(1-\frac a2,
    21	  \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right).
    22	\end{equation}
    23	The strict intervals are nonempty. The $C^\theta$ norm is the supremum norm plus
    24	the $\theta$-H\"older seminorm.

    56	\subsection{A test basis and explicit covariance coefficients}
    57	
    58	\begin{lemma}[Basis in the prescribed quotient]\label{L:driver-noise-basis}
    59	  The nonzero space $H_W$ is separable and infinite-dimensional. It has a real
    60	  orthonormal basis with compact smooth representatives, whose evaluations by
    61	  $W$ are independent standard real Gaussians.
    62	\end{lemma}
    63	
    64	\begin{proof}
    65	  For tests supported in $[0,L]\times K$, with $K$ compact, the physical
    66	  covariance and the temporal Schur bound give the absolute estimate
    67	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-test-continuity}
    68	    |\langle F,G\rangle_{H_W}|
    69	    \le |K|\Gamma(K-K)\frac{2L^{1-a}}{1-a}
    70	    \|\|F(t)\|_\infty\|_{L^2(0,L)}
    71	    \|\|G(t)\|_\infty\|_{L^2(0,L)}.
    72	  \end{equation}
    73	  Only spatial differences in $K-K$ contribute. On each rational compact box
    74	  inside positive time, rational step approximations followed by compact smooth
    75	  mollifiers at rational scales give a countable uniformly dense test
    76	  collection, supported in a fixed slightly larger box. The estimate proves
    77	  noise-norm approximation. The union over increasing boxes is dense in the test
    78	  completion. This proves separability without assuming the covariance form is
    79	  injective.
    80	
    81	  Choose $L \ge 1$ with $0 < \Gamma(B_L) < \infty$ and nonnegative compact
    82	  smooth $q \ge 1$ on $B_{2L+1}$. Then
    83	  \[
    84	    Q_{\rm sp}:=\int\Gamma(\ud y)\int q(x)q(x-y)\ud x
    85	    \ge |B_{L+1}|\Gamma(B_L)>0,
    86	  \]
    87	  and the compact-support estimate makes it finite. For every real compact
    88	  smooth positive-time $\tau$, the tensor identity is
    89	  \[
    90	    \|\tau\otimes q\|_{H_W}^2=Q_{\rm sp}\|\tau\|_a^2.
    91	  \]
    92	  Here the temporal norm is computed on any finite interval containing the
    93	  support of $\tau$. It is strictly positive for signed nonzero $\tau$. Indeed,
    94	  zero-extend this deterministic test and use the positive Laplace factorization
    95	  from Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} to write
    96	  \begin{align*}
    97	    \|\tau\|_a^2
    98	    &=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}\int_0^\infty\lambda^{a-1}
    99	    E_\lambda(\tau)\ud\lambda,\\
   100	    E_\lambda(\tau)
   101	    &=\int_\R 2\lambda\left|\int_r^\infty
   102	    e^{-\lambda(t-r)}\tau(t)\ud t\right|^2\ud r.
   103	  \end{align*}
   104	  Signed exchanges are absolutely integrable on the test support, by the
   105	  temporal Schur estimate. If the norm vanished, some $\lambda > 0$ would have
   106	  $E_\lambda = 0$. Its inner integral $v(r)$ is continuous and satisfies $v' =
   107	  \lambda v-\tau$. Vanishing almost everywhere makes it identically zero and
   108	  forces $\tau = 0$. Thus, infinitely many linearly independent compact time
   109	  bumps inject into $H_W$ after multiplication by $q$.
   110	
   111	  Apply Gram--Schmidt to a countable dense real test collection, discarding zero
   112	  residuals in the given null quotient. Infinitude gives an infinite basis; each
   113	  representative is a finite linear combination of compact smooth tests. The
   114	  isonormal identity gives $\E g_jg_k = \delta_{jk}$. Joint Gaussian
   115	  characteristic functions then factor, giving independence and unit variances.
   116	  No physical null direction is removed beyond the prescribed quotient, and no
   117	  $H_W$-valued white Gaussian vector is used. This proves
   118	  Lemma~\ref{L:driver-noise-basis}.
   119	\end{proof}
   120	
   121	\begin{lemma}[Covariance coefficients]\label{L:driver-covariance-coefficients}
   122	  For each basis representative put
   123	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-covariance-coefficient}
   124	    H_{j,R}(t,x)=\zeta_R(x)\int_{u>0}|t-u|^{-a}
   125	    \int\Gamma(\ud y)f_j(u,x-y)\ud u.
   126	  \end{equation}
   127	  These functions are real smooth on finite time-space compacts, supported
   128	  spatially in $B_{2R}$, with bounded derivatives there. For smooth compact real
   129	  positive-time $F$, and also for the admitted wave tests
   130	  of~\eqref{E:variance-actual-form},
   131	  \begin{equation}\label{E:driver-literal-covariance}
   132	    \E[W_{\mathbb{C}}(\zeta_RF)g_j]
   133	    =\int H_{j,R}(t,x)F(t,x)\ud t\ud x.
   134	  \end{equation}
   135	  The coefficient on $t \ge 0$ depends only on the $H_W$ class of $f_j$.
   136	\end{lemma}
   137	
   138	\begin{proof}
   139	  Extend $f_j$ smoothly by zero in time and substitute $v = t-u$. The unmasked
   140	  expression is $\int_\R |v|^{-a}\int\Gamma(\ud y)f_j(t-v,x-y)\ud v$. On each
   141	  compact $(t,x)$ set, the integrand involves only bounded $v$ and a common
   142	  compact set of $y$. Local Radon mass and local integrability of $|v|^{-a}$
   143	  allow every mixed derivative to move onto the smooth test. Dominated
   144	  integration proves smoothness and the derivative bounds. Multiplication by
   145	  $\zeta_R$ gives the stated support. Zero extension is only of a deterministic
   146	  test; no negative-time noise is introduced.
   147	
   148	  The physical covariance formula and absolute Fubini give
   149	  \eqref{E:driver-literal-covariance} first for real compact tests. The compact
   150	  difference set in $\Gamma$ and integrable temporal singularity justify the
   151	  exchange. For wave tests use the common-support original approximations of
   152	  Proposition~\ref{P:actual-wave-form}, converging in $L^2$ time in the spatial
   153	  supremum norm after masking. The left side converges by noise Cauchy--Schwarz
   154	  and the right side by the coefficient's boundedness on that support. Real and
   155	  imaginary parts give the complex version. If two representatives give the same
   156	  class, their Gaussian difference is zero. Testing the covariance identity
   157	  against every compact smooth $F$ makes the difference of their masked
   158	  coefficients zero as a distribution for $t > 0$. Smoothness, then continuity
   159	  at zero, proves the representative assertion on $t \ge 0$. This proves
   160	  Lemma~\ref{L:driver-covariance-coefficients}.
   161	\end{proof}
